## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uposathāvimānavatthu* (Vv 24) is a verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [Lim 2009]. Structured around a question-and-answer exchange between the Venerable Mahā-Moggallāna and an enskied female deva, the text recounts the past human life of the laywoman Uposathā [Lim 2009]. Having frequently heard descriptions of the heavenly Nandana grove, she set her mind upon it with longing (*tattha cittaṃ paṇidhāya*), which resulted in her rebirth in that celestial realm [Lim 2009]. However, she expresses regret for having aimed her mind at an inferior destination (*hīne cittaṃ paṇidhāya*) instead of cultivating it further toward higher spiritual attainments [Lim 2009]. Modern scholarship has examined the text as an illustration of the operation of resolve and aspiration (*paṇidhi*) in early Buddhist rebirth doctrine [Lim 2009].

The text shares extensive formulaic and verse material across the Pali canon and commentaries.
